nodes.title: Dense optical flow: every algorithm, four views
widgets_values:
Optical flow playground - every DENSE algorithm the pack exposes, on one frame pair, through four shared debug views.

THE ALGORITHMS (left column, top to bottom)
* Farneback - polynomial expansion, the classic. Curated node.
* DIS - Dense Inverse Search: patch matching, propagation, then a variational polish. Faster AND sharper than Farneback; the default choice. Shown three times: the medium preset, the same with the refinement turned OFF (blockier), and that raw field pushed through 'CV Refine Flow (Variational)' as an explicit step - which is what lets the refinement be applied to ANY field, including Farneback's.
* TV-L1 - L1 data term + total-variation prior. The accuracy reference of the classic methods and the sharpest at motion boundaries; also ~10x slower than DIS.
* RLOF (dense) - tracks a GRID of points with an illumination-robust local solver, then interpolates them (EPIC/RIC/GEO). The one to reach for when the two frames differ in EXPOSURE. Needs colour.
* DeepFlow - descriptor matching before the variational solve, so it follows LARGE displacements.
* PCAFlow - projection onto a learned basis: fast and noise-immune, but it can only express motion its basis contains (watch it under-shoot the fast vehicles).
* SimpleFlow / SparseToDense - raw cv2 function wrappers, so they output a bare flow array with no magnitude/angle of their own. SimpleFlow returns NaNs (~4% of the frame here) - see the debug branch.

Everything from TV-L1 down is a cv2 CLASS rather than a plain function, so it comes as a curated node instead of a raw cv2.* wrapper.

THE PATTERN
'CreateList' collects all ten fields into one LIST, and every node after it runs once per item - so each debug view below is ONE chain, not ten. Captions come from a single ';'-separated string through 'RegexSplitDataList' -> 'Draw Text' (the sheet pattern from 18_inpainting_playground). Add an algorithm = one node + one label.

THE FOUR VIEWS
1. Direction sheet - 'Flow To Color': hue = angle, brightness = speed.
2. Magnitude sheet - speed as GRAYSCALE (cv2.normalize MINMAX -> 8-bit). Each tile is normalized to ITS OWN max, so tiles are not comparable in absolute terms - the heatmap preview next to it keeps the colour scale.
3. Arrow grid - the classic quiver plot over frame A.
4. Warp error - remap frame B BACKWARDS through the flow and take |A - warped|. This is the only view that says whether a field is RIGHT rather than merely plausible: a correct flow makes the moving objects disappear, and whatever stays bright is where that algorithm failed. Note the arithmetic: cv2.remap needs absolute coordinates, so the flow is ADDED to an Identity Map.

Also here: 'Inspect CV Data' on the list prints dtype/shape/min/max per algorithm (that is how the SimpleFlow NaNs show up), and the magnitude heatmap uses 'Preview CV Array' in heatmap mode with the colour scale on. Sparse tracking is a different shape of output and lives elsewhere ('CV Track Features (KLT)', exercise_visual_odometry).

Try: swap the two LoadImage nodes for any pair of your own frames; raise RLOF's grid_step for speed; switch its interpolation to RIC for the sharpest boundaries; lower TV-L1's lambda_ for a smoother field.
